incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming-edge in eu-west-2. SLO breach: streaming.p99 > 6s over last 5m. Auto-created incident #INC-2026-761.
Alice K: acked, taking initial lead. paging eu-west2 oncall.
Alice K: any customer-facing impact yet?
CS Bot: customer X and Y report intermittent reconnections, session dropouts ~8-12s.
Ben L: joining — network oncall. seeing spikes across inter-zone NAT paths.
Carol S: bringing up dashboards. graph: streaming-tail (p99) jump at 5229987000 -> 5229990000.
Dave M: quick check of NAT metrics: SNAT port exhaustion trend up since 5229975000. ephemeral_port_usage ~ 96%.
Eve SRE: possible NAT table/conntrack backpressure too. 
Alice K: plan: 1) validate NAT ephemeral pool saturation 2) temporary egress steer to alternate AZ 3) customer mitigation (scale fallback) 4) longer-term fix.
Ben L: running quick probe across AZs for handshake RTTs: 
```
for az in azb azc azd; do curl -s -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null https://edge-eu-west2.local; done
```
Ben L: results show AZB->AZC RTT increase and failed TLS handshakes around 5229989000.
Carol S: logs snippet (filtered to session id): 
```
[5229989103] tls_handshake_timeout src=10.2.4.5 dst=54.239.1.2 sni=edge-eu-west2
[5229989110] conntrack_retry_limit src=10.2.4.5
```
Alice K: @Ben please try ephemeral pool expand and add a temporary NAT SNAT rule with larger port range in eu-west-2. Notify infra before change.
Ben L: doing `aws ec2 modify-nat-gateway` style patch for managed NAT — will also open a short burst capacity on dedicated NAT nodes.
Dave M: if we can’t expand fast enough, we can steer egress for streaming traffic to AZ with spare NAT capacity via iptables SNAT in the edge proxies.
Eve SRE: coordinating a canary reroute for 10% of traffic to eu-west-2b with `traffic-router` override.
Product Pager: are we affecting non-streaming APIs?
Carol S: embeddings and non-streaming endpoints show normal p95; this is streaming-edge specific — points to long-lived connections and ephemeral port exhaustion.
Ben L: NAT port pool expanded +20% at 5229990800. monitoring...
Alice K: spinning up temporary dedicated proxies in eu-west-2b and will steer 30% of streaming route there.
Ben L: steer applied at 5229991400 via `traffic-router set-route --streaming=eu-west-2b --weight=30%`.
CS Bot: customer X reports drop rate improved from 12% -> 5% after initial steer.
Eve SRE: metrics show streaming.p99 decreased from ~8.5s -> 3.2s after steer. p95 stable.
Alice K: good. keep monitoring for 15m. we'll keep incident open for root cause and followup.
Ben L: noticed abnormal DNS latencies upstream during the spike — several NXDOMAIN/timeout bursts. Could be overloaded resolver path compounding handshake delays.
Carol S: capturing packet samples for 5229989000-5229992000. attaching pcap to ticket INC-2026-761.
Dave M: quick kernel tuning applied on proxies (tcp_tw_reuse=1, ip_local_port_range widened) at 5229992100 to reduce TIME_WAIT hold.
Alice K: are we comfortable with these transient kernel tweaks? any risk to control plane?
Ben L: low risk, revert after traffic normalizes.
Eve SRE: oncall handoff — I'm going offline in 25m. Ben, do you want primary?
Ben L: I can take primary until root cause triage complete. Alice, Ben, Carol will form core RCA team.
Alice K: accepted handoff. updating incident channel and performing customer impact note for status page.
Product Pager: drafting status-page message: "We are investigating elevated streaming latency in eu-west-2 affecting long-lived streaming sessions. Mitigation in progress: traffic reroute and NAT capacity increase. Customers may see intermittent reconnects."
CS Bot: Sent targeted DM to top 10 customers affected with temporary workaround (client-side reconnect backoff suggested).
Carol S: initial hypothesis: bursty connection churn + upstream DNS/TLS handshake amplification -> NAT ephemeral port exhaustion -> connection stalls -> streaming tail blowups. Need full packet-level trace + NAT flow table logs to confirm.
Dave M: next actions: 1) preserve NAT flow tables 2) get resolver logs from provider 3) run synthetic long-lived connection soak test in staging to reproduce.
Ben L: saving counters and exporting conntrack state to S3 at 5229993000.
Alice K: ETA for full mitigation if no regressions? Ben/Eve/Dave?
Ben L: with current steps, risk of recurrence low but keep scaling headroom for next 2 hours. Recommend follow-up: permanent SNAT pool increase + egress multipath policy.
Eve SRE: we'll schedule a postmortem and include action items: NAT autoscale runbooks, resolver fallbacks, hardened edge proxy configs.
Alice K: thanks everyone. leaving notes in INC ticket and will convert to a postmortem template. once streaming.p99 < 1s for 30m we'll mark as mitigated.
incidents-bot: Incident #INC-2026-761 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring.
Ben L: final check at 5229994600 shows p99 ~0.9s, no new handshake timeouts. closing active paging.
Alice K: closing thread for active mitigation. will re-open if any regression. retrospective to be scheduled tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
